blocks.text:
## What to Expect

The first days focus on Quito and the northern Andes. Discover the capital's historic centre, ride the cable car towards Rucu Pichincha, and visit Otavalo, Cotacachi, Peguche Waterfall, Cuicocha Crater Lake and the high-altitude El Ángel Reserve.

The journey then takes you to the Equator Line, the Intiñán Museum and the Pululahua Geobotanical Reserve. The scenery becomes greener as you enter Bellavista's cloud forest for birdwatching, visit Escondida Waterfall and Mindo, and explore Yanacocha Reserve.

Next come Cotopaxi and Quilotoa Crater Lake. The final major portion of the journey takes place in the Amazon at Sacha Lodge, where activities include motorised and paddle canoe trips, walks through the jungle, birdwatching and wildlife spotting, a walkway above the forest canopy, night excursions, lakes and flooded forest.

## How the Journey Works

The itinerary covers several ecological zones, with the landscape changing markedly as you travel. Quito lies at approximately 2,800 m; the upper TelefériQo station is around 4,100 m, while the northern Andean reserves include páramo habitats and Polylepis forests. After the highlands, the route descends into cloud forest, returns to the volcanic region and finally continues into the Amazon Basin.

Some days involve substantial travel and activities. The Yanacocha day, including transfers, takes around eight hours; the length of the hiking day at Quilotoa depends on the chosen activities. The Amazon section also involves early starts, boats, forest walks and wildlife watching after dark.

Several forms of transport are used: private road transfers, a boat on Cuicocha, the Quito cable car, and motorised and paddle canoes in the Amazon. Certain nature excursions require walking, and the order of individual activities may be adjusted for the weather and guests' fitness levels.

Excursions in Bellavista and the Amazon are shared with other travellers; other parts of the journey are private. An English-speaking guide accompanies the Amazon activities, while English-speaking guiding or driver-guide services are provided on the mainland.

There are calendar restrictions. The rose plantation is closed to visitors on weekends and public holidays. Sacha Lodge does not accept arrivals or departures on Sundays. The tour may begin on any day, subject to availability of excursions and hotel accommodation.

## Practical Route Details

Accommodation changes as the journey moves between ecological zones: a city hotel in Quito, historic haciendas, Polylepis Lodge, Bellavista Lodge and Sacha Lodge in the Amazon. This keeps you closer to the natural areas visited early in the morning or late in the day.

Meals included depend on the day. Some hotels include breakfast only, while Bellavista and much of the Amazon stay include breakfast, lunch and dinner. Boxed lunches are provided on certain full-day excursions.

Some optional activities depend on a group decision. For example, the descent to Quilotoa Lake and a kayaking outing may be chosen if conditions permit. Returning uphill by mule is also charged separately and depends on local availability.

Birdwatching excursions begin early, when many species are most active. At Bellavista, the departure to observe Andean cocks-of-the-rock is scheduled for approximately 05:00; the morning walk at Yanacocha starts at around 06:00; and at Sacha Lodge some excursions start between 06:00 and 07:00.

The Amazon section involves several transfers. After the flight to Coca, continue by motorised canoe, then walk through the forest and cross a lake by paddle canoe. The return trip follows the same route in reverse.

## Programme Prices

The price per person depends on the room arrangement:

| Room arrangement | Price, USD |
|---|---:|
| Triple (TPL) | 7,443 |
| Double (DBL) | 7,999 |
| Single, for a solo traveller (SGL) | 12,775 |

The single-room supplement for a traveller in a group of at least two is USD 1,546. The Quito–Coca–Quito flight is charged separately. Hotels, availability and the final price are confirmed upon booking.
